query: Microsoft fiscal year 2026 Q1 AI capital expenditure data center spending
normalized: 2026 ai capital center data expenditure fiscal microsoft q1 spending year

output.content:
**Microsoft FY2026 Q1 AI/data-center spending** — for the quarter ended **September 30, 2025**, Microsoft reported **$34.9 billion of capital expenditures**, explicitly attributing the spend to demand for its cloud and AI offerings. [[1]]

- About **half of total capex**—approximately **$17.5 billion**—went to short-lived assets, principally GPUs and CPUs, supporting Azure demand, first-party applications and AI solutions, internal R&D, and replacement of end-of-life server/network equipment. [[1]]
- The other approximately **$17.5 billion** was long-lived infrastructure expected to support monetization for 15 years or more; this included **$11.1 billion of finance leases**, primarily for large data-center sites. [[1]]
- Cash payments for property, plant and equipment were **$19.4 billion**, versus $14.9 billion in FY2025 Q1; the difference between the $34.9 billion capex measure and cash PP&E payments chiefly reflected finance leases and the timing of equipment receipts versus payment. [[1]] [[2]]
- On Microsoft’s cash-flow statement, reported additions to property and equipment were **$19.394 billion**, a **30.0% year-over-year** increase from **$14.923 billion**. [[2]]
- On the broader management capex definition, the **$34.9 billion** was **74.5% higher year over year** than the **$20.0 billion** reported in FY2025 Q1, which also included finance leases. [[1]] [[3]]
- The Q1 figure equaled roughly **44.9% of quarterly revenue** of $77.673 billion, underscoring the unusually capital-intensive nature of Microsoft’s AI capacity buildout. [[4]] [[1]]
- Microsoft also disclosed **$106.2 billion of additional, not-yet-commenced leases**, primarily for data centers, as of September 30, 2025; those leases are scheduled to commence between FY2026 and FY2031. [[5]]
- Management said it planned to increase total AI capacity by **more than 80% in FY2026** and to **roughly double its total data-center footprint over the subsequent two years**. [[1]]
- For the following quarter, Microsoft guided that total capex would rise sequentially and that FY2026 capex growth would exceed FY2025’s growth rate, citing accelerating demand, a growing RPO balance, and increased GPU/CPU spending. [[1]] 

The key analytical distinction is that **$34.9 billion is companywide capex including finance leases**, rather than a pure AI-only or pure data-center number; however, management directly tied the spending mix to cloud and AI capacity, and specifically identified the $11.1 billion finance-lease component as primarily large data-center sites. [[1]]
